title: Vienna in 3 days: palaces, Klimt and coffee houses
author: Brogan
intro: Three days is the right amount of time for Vienna: one for the old centre and the Hofburg, one for Schönbrunn and the Belvedere, and one for markets, museums and the Prater. Here's how to fit it together.
seo_title: Vienna in 3 days: itinerary, palaces and tips
seo_description: Day 1 the old centre and Hofburg, day 2 Schönbrunn and Klimt's The Kiss, day 3 museums and the Prater. A 3-day Vienna plan with transport tips.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Day 1:** Old centre and Hofburg
- **Day 2:** Schönbrunn and Belvedere
- **Day 3:** Museums, market, Prater
- **Flight from London:** about 2¼ hours
- **Airport train:** about 16 minutes

[Vienna](/destinations/vienna) is compact, clean and easy to get around, with a public transport network that reaches every sight in this plan. The centre is walkable; the two big palaces are a short tram or underground ride out.

sections.heading: The 3-day plan at a glance
sections.text:
| Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | St Stephen's Cathedral | Hofburg and the Spanish Riding School | Coffee house, then the opera |
| 2 | Schönbrunn Palace | Belvedere and The Kiss | Dinner in a Heuriger wine tavern |
| 3 | MuseumsQuartier or Kunsthistorisches | Naschmarkt | Giant Ferris wheel at the Prater |

If you're there between mid-November and Christmas, swap any evening for the Christmas markets, the biggest of which fills the square in front of the city hall.

sections.heading: Day 1: the old centre and the Hofburg
sections.text:
Start at St Stephen's Cathedral, with its patterned tiled roof, in the very middle of the old town. Climb the south tower for the view, or take the lift up the north tower.

From there, walk along the Graben and Kohlmarkt to the Hofburg, the Habsburgs' huge winter palace. Inside are the imperial apartments, the Sisi Museum and the silver collection, and the Spanish Riding School, where the white Lipizzaner horses train.

- **Coffee house:** stop at one of the classic Viennese cafés for coffee and a slice of Sachertorte or apple strudel.
- **Evening:** the State Opera sells cheap standing tickets on the day for many performances, a famous Vienna bargain.

Tip: the Spanish Riding School sells tickets to watch the horses' morning exercise, which is far cheaper than a full performance. Check the dates, as it doesn't run every day.

sections.heading: Day 2: Schönbrunn and the Belvedere
sections.text:
Schönbrunn Palace, the Habsburgs' summer residence, is on the U4 underground line, about 15 minutes from the centre. Book a timed ticket for the state rooms, then walk up through the gardens to the Gloriette for the view back over the palace and the city.

In the afternoon, head to the Belvedere, two baroque palaces facing each other across formal gardens. The Upper Belvedere holds the world's biggest collection of Gustav Klimt's paintings, including The Kiss. In the evening, take a tram out to the edge of the city to a Heuriger, a traditional wine tavern in the vineyards, where winemakers serve their own new wine.

sections.heading: Day 3: museums, markets and the Prater
sections.text:
Vienna has more great museums than you can see in a day, so pick one or two:

- **Kunsthistorisches Museum:** old masters, including the world's largest collection of paintings by Pieter Bruegel the Elder.
- **MuseumsQuartier:** modern art at the Leopold Museum, with its Schiele collection, and MUMOK.
- **Natural History Museum:** across the square from the Kunsthistorisches, with the Venus of Willendorf.

At lunchtime, walk to the Naschmarkt, the city's long open-air market, for food stalls and cafés. End the trip at the Prater, a big park with a funfair and the Riesenrad, the giant Ferris wheel from 1897, which has wooden cabins and great views at dusk.

Local knowledge: many museums close one day a week, often Monday. Check opening days before you plan day 3.

sections.heading: Getting there and getting around
sections.text:
Vienna is about two and a quarter hours' flight from London, with direct flights from several UK airports. The City Airport Train runs non-stop to Wien Mitte in about 16 minutes. The S-Bahn takes a little longer but costs much less.

- **Getting around:** a 24, 48 or 72-hour pass covers the underground, trams and buses.
- **Money:** Austria uses the euro.
- **Where to stay:** inside or just outside the Ring, the boulevard around the old town, puts everything in this plan within easy reach.
- **Add a city:** [Bratislava](/destinations/bratislava) is an hour away, and [Budapest](/blog/budapest-in-3-days) and [Prague](/blog/prague-in-3-days) are easy by train.

sections.heading: When to go
sections.text:
May, June and September are warm and green, and the Danube Island is good for swimming. July and August can be hot, and many locals leave the city.

From mid-November to Christmas, Vienna is one of the best Christmas market cities in Europe. Our post on [Vienna or Prague at Christmas](/blog/vienna-or-prague-at-christmas) compares the two, and [best Christmas markets in Europe](/blog/best-christmas-markets-in-europe) has the 2026 dates.

For more short trips, see our [3-day city break](/blog/best-places-for-a-3-day-city-break-in-europe) post. If you can't agree where to go next, put a few cities in a draw on [somewhere.party](/).

faqs.question: Is 3 days enough for Vienna?
faqs.answer: Yes. Three days gives you time for the old centre and the Hofburg, Schönbrunn and the Belvedere, and a day of museums and the Prater.

faqs.question: How do you get from Vienna airport to the city centre?
faqs.answer: The City Airport Train runs non-stop to Wien Mitte in about 16 minutes. The S-Bahn is slower but cheaper.

faqs.question: Where can you see Klimt's The Kiss?
faqs.answer: At the Upper Belvedere in Vienna, which has the world's largest collection of Klimt's paintings.

faqs.question: Should you book Schönbrunn Palace in advance?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tickets for the state rooms are for a set time, and they often sell out on busy days, so book online.
